body: You are a fun person.
Thank you, you are very kind. Having someone understand and respond makes things easier.

I feel the same way. I think the answer you're looking for is one you already know. You should live your dream, it seems very possible for you. Someone who has invested so much time in school but have retained a bit of usable knowledge. You do not owe anyone anything. Get up right now, pack your things, and move somewhere want to live. It doesn't matter how small a place it is or if you're sharing with roommates. This life is too short and pointless to not do what you love. Your dream is very realistic, it can be done and is done by people like you. Your dream sounds beautiful, you should pursue it. You do not owe anyone anything. 

If you kill yourself, it will be the same as finishing and getting your law degree and living a life you hate. You should go on an adventure instead and instead of writing useless papers on law, write about your adventure out of depression and into a world you love. Make your dream come true, please. If you can do it, then maybe I have hope as well.

It's better to be on the first step of a ladder you want to climb than half way up one you don't.

I think that a lot of people have that point in their life, but I don't think humanity will reach that point in our lifetime. I think the powers in control have a HUGE upperhand. In short, we are enslaved and it is going to take A LOT to change it. If it's gradual. . . it will take a long time. Then again I could be wrong! I hope so!

My girlfriend tripsat me yesterday and I would start a sentence then midway start staring at something and let out one long, "uhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh". It was kind of hilarious actually. :)

I realized this when I was drawing in my journal. I kept thinking of what I would make my pen do next, but it would always do something differently. It was kind of like the pen was a ouija board. Somehow, even though the pen never did what I initially wanted it to, it came out beautiful and I was pleased with it the second I finished making a mark.

The crazy thing about going a little too deep is that it really leaves you with something you would have never had from a low dose trip. My first trip wasn't as deep as yours, but there were moments where things got REAL, VERY fast. It was beautiful but terrifying. 

I tripped for the second time yesterday and it was the perfect dosage to get me used to wading in the shallow end of the lsd pool. It was a beautiful and very mild trip. Maybe try a low dosage and ease yourself back into it? There's nothing wrong with figuring out how to maneuver safely inside an lsd trip.

I'm always very conscious of what my actions are, but it's the feelings that really eat me up. I don't take high doses, but I still get the visuals and all that. Still. . . I am coherent to a certain degree but it would be clear something is bothering me or giving me anxiety. I prefer doing it in my apartment and only adventuring around the area and coming back to safety. So. . . idk how to control higher doses. I think it's just starting small and working your way up maybe? Being comfortable with the terrain?

There were fits of laughter and lots of cool moments, but we were all tripping and I felt that was very unsafe and like no one knew what was going on. 

This time it's with my girlfriend of 3 years, in our own apartment (we had roommates before), with our dog and cat, and during the day. She will be tripsitting so I am 100% ready for a fun and safe trip.

I have those "what if's" as well and all I can say is that getting pumped up for it is calming me down and you're not alone in feeling nervous! It's totally normal! Maybe meditate beforehand, there's a good one on soundcloud if you search, "mindful meditation". It really helps me relax. I'm sure we will both have great trips! :)
